events.text: Code and tests are written. Running the test suite:
Everything passes, including the race detector. Now I'll record before/after demos for reviewers.

POST /todos now validates its input, returns JSON errors, and rate-limits each client, all with the standard library only. `go vet` is clean and all 26 tests pass under `-race`. I haven't committed anything.

**Validation** (`main.go`)
- **Title:** required. It's trimmed first, so `"   "` counts as missing, and stored trimmed. The 200-character limit counts characters rather than bytes, so 200 × `é` is accepted.
- **Unknown fields:** rejected. I decode into a separate request type that only has `title` and `done`, so a client-sent `id` is also rejected instead of quietly ignored.
- **Body:** must be exactly one JSON object of at most 1 MiB. Content-Type must be `application/json`, otherwise the response is 415.

**Errors** always look like `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}` with a JSON content type. The codes are `validation_failed`, `unknown_field`, `invalid_json`, `body_too_large` (413), `unsupported_media_type` (415) and `rate_limited` (429).

**Rate limiting** (`ratelimit.go`): each client IP can send a burst of 10 requests, refilled at 5 per second. Over the limit it returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Idle clients are dropped after 5 minutes so memory doesn't keep growing. Rejected requests also count toward the limit.

**Tests** (`main_test.go`, `ratelimit_test.go`) cover every rejection case, the success path, refill, per-IP isolation and cleanup. They use a fake clock, so they don't sleep.

**grasp:** no earlier feedback was waiting. I recorded four decisions and two before/after demos:
- **Bad bodies:** they returned 201 and stored junk like `{"id":1,"title":""}`; now they get a 400 with an error code.
- **Rate limit:** requests 11 and 12 of a burst now get 429; before, every request returned 201.

**Before you deploy:**
- **Behind a proxy or load balancer,** every client shares the proxy's IP and therefore one limit. I didn't trust `X-Forwarded-For` because clients can fake it. That needs handling for trusted proxies first.
- **The limit is per instance,** so with several replicas the real total is that many times higher.
- **Clients that send extra fields or no Content-Type** will start getting 400 or 415.
- **The server has no read or write timeouts** (`ReadHeaderTimeout` etc.), so slow clients can tie up connections. I left that out to keep this change to POST /todos; it's a small follow-up.

decisions.title: Strict validation of POST /todos body
decisions.why: Right now the handler ignores decode errors and stores whatever arrives. Decoding into a separate request struct {title, done} with DisallowUnknownFields means id and any typo'd field get rejected. Title is trimmed and must be 1–200 characters (counted as runes, not bytes). Body is capped at 1 MiB, must be a single JSON object, and must be sent as application/json.
alternatives: Decode straight into Todo (then a client could send id, and 'id' wouldn't count as unknown)
Count the 200 limit in bytes (would reject valid non-ASCII titles that are under 200 characters)
Don't check Content-Type (more lenient, but form posts and other content types slip through)
decisions.risk: Clients that currently send extra fields, or that leave out Content-Type, will start getting 400/415.

decisions.title: Uniform JSON error envelope
decisions.why: Every error from POST /todos returns {"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}} with Content-Type application/json, so clients can branch on a stable code and don't have to parse text. Success responses get the JSON content type too.
alternatives: RFC 7807 problem+json (more fields than this API needs)
decisions.risk: Low. The error shape becomes part of the API contract.

decisions.title: Per-IP token bucket on POST /todos
decisions.why: Each client gets a token bucket keyed by the RemoteAddr host: 5 requests/second with a burst of 10. Over the limit it returns 429 with Retry-After. Buckets idle for more than a few minutes are swept so memory can't grow without bound. A clock can be injected so tests are deterministic.
alternatives: golang.org/x/time/rate (not stdlib; user asked for stdlib only)
Key on X-Forwarded-For (clients can spoof it unless we're behind a trusted proxy)
Fixed-window counter (allows 2x bursts at window edges)
decisions.risk: Behind a load balancer or reverse proxy, every request shares the proxy's IP, so all clients would share one bucket. That needs trusted-proxy header handling before deploying behind one. State lives in memory per instance, so the limit applies per replica, not globally.

decisions.title: Handler tests with httptest and fake clock
decisions.why: Table-driven tests run against the real mux (newServer) using httptest. They cover each validation rule, the error envelope, and rate limiting (burst, 429 plus Retry-After, refill, per-IP isolation, eviction). A fake clock means no sleeps.
alternatives: Spin up a real listener (slower, no added coverage)

behaviors.title: Invalid POST /todos bodies are rejected
behaviors.command: go build -o /tmp/todoapi_demo . && (/tmp/todoapi_demo & echo $! > /tmp/todoapi_demo.pid); sleep 1; for b in '{"done":true}' '{"title":"x","priority":1}' '{"id":99,"title":"x"}' '{"title":'; do printf '%s -> ' "$b"; curl -s -w ' [%{http_code}]\n' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$b" localhost:8080/todos; done; kill $(cat /tmp/todoapi_demo.pid)
behaviors.expect: Each body gets a 400 with a JSON error (validation_failed, unknown_field, unknown_field, invalid_json). The old code returns 201 and stores junk todos.

behaviors.title: Burst past 10 requests gets 429
behaviors.command: go build -o /tmp/todoapi_demo . && (/tmp/todoapi_demo & echo $! > /tmp/todoapi_demo.pid); sleep 1; for i in $(seq 1 12); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"x"}' localhost:8080/todos; done; echo; curl -s -i -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"x"}' localhost:8080/todos | grep -iE '^HTTP|^retry-after|error'; kill $(cat /tmp/todoapi_demo.pid)
behaviors.expect: The first 10 requests return 201 and the rest 429. The final request shows HTTP 429, Retry-After: 1, and a rate_limited JSON error. The old code returns 201 every time.
